comparison: Both evaluate DeePosit's core performance metrics (C8, C26, C36, C38, C40-C43, C45, C47-C48, C50-C51, C54) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed quantitative validation, while peer reviewers affirm 'solid evidence' with 'accuracy near 90%'. Both also address practical advantages (C10-C11, C83-C84, C135), with peer reviewers noting the tool will be 'useful' for many assays.

Perfect agreement on sex-dependent differences in CD1 mice (C72-C82). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed statistical validation from Figure 6 and Table 1, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings as part of the broader validated methodology without raising concerns.

Perfect agreement on behavioral validation claims (C28-C33). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites quantitative data from Figure 1 with statistical tests, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these control behaviors as appropriate context, focusing their attention on the detection method rather than questioning these results.

Perfect agreement on spatial preference findings (C132-C134). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this is a negative finding appropriately compared to prior work, while peer reviewers accept this honest reporting without challenge, consistent with their general acceptance of the methodology.

Disagreement on error impact claims (C93-C103, especially C102-C103). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED, stating errors should not create systematic bias. Peer reviewers evaluate as UNCERTAIN, with the second reviewer explicitly concerned that '~10% error rate might miss subtle biological effects' and 'may be too low to detect some effects that are biologically real but subtle.'

Both evaluate temporal dynamics findings (C9, C27, C55-C62, C65) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed validation of the two-peak urination vs. single-peak defecation patterns with statistical tests. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these biological patterns, with the first reviewer acknowledging the method's importance for studying 'key ethological behaviors.'

Both evaluate strain difference findings (C66-C71, C127-C131) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval documents quantitative comparisons between CD1 and C57BL/6 mice with appropriate acknowledgment of smaller C57BL/6 sample size. Peer reviewers do not challenge these findings, accepting them as part of the broader validated results.

Both address mechanistic interpretations (C113-C120, C122). OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN, noting that while temporal patterns are clearly shown, mechanistic interpretations remain speculative. Peer reviewers evaluate as SUPPORTED but focus on the observed patterns rather than mechanistic claims, implicitly accepting the descriptive findings.

Partial overlap on practical advantages and generalizability (C85-C88 in both, C89-C90, C136-C137 in peer R5). OpenEval evaluates practical advantages as SUPPORTED based on demonstrated capabilities. Peer reviewers evaluate broader applicability as UNCERTAIN, noting 'training and testing for specific contexts used by other experimenters is probably warranted,' tempering generalizability claims.

Both address thermal imaging methodology (C34-C35, C93). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED, citing well-established physics and clear demonstrations. Peer reviewers also evaluate as SUPPORTED, describing it as 'an important machine-learning-based approach' and accepting the thermal imaging methodology as valid.

Both address future applications and generalizability (C89-C90, C136-C137). OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are appropriately speculative claims not demonstrated in the current study. Peer reviewers also express UNCERTAINTY about generalizability, specifically noting the need for context-specific training and testing.

Both address YOLOv8 comparison (C48, C104-C105). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED with quantitative comparison from Figure 3h-j, though notes the comparison is somewhat limited. Peer reviewers include these claims in their SUPPORTED evaluation of overall performance, accepting the comparative validation.

OpenEval evaluates future improvement directions (C106-C112) as SUPPORTED, noting they are appropriately framed as speculative and based on identified limitations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific technical improvement suggestions.

OpenEval evaluates background knowledge claims about scent marking (C1-C3, C12-C17) as SUPPORTED, noting these are well-established facts with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on novel findings rather than background context.

OpenEval evaluates limitations of prior methods (C4, C18-C22, C25) as SUPPORTED, noting these are well-known issues that motivate the study. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on the new method's performance rather than critiquing prior approaches.
